review.evidenceBasis: Checked every mapping row of the 6-row draft against the cie-igcse-further-maths-additional-maths-25 spine, judging each of the 8 (video,spec) bindings independently. Rejected 5 spec-level bindings: both linear-inequality videos off 2.5.1/2.5.2 (spec 2.5 is quadratic inequalities; the example forms '–3 < x < 4' and 'x < 1 or x > 6' are solution-set shapes, not compound-linear topics) and the physics resultant-forces video off 13.3.2 (vector geometry ≠ force resultants). Kept the three rows whose titles name the spec's own body: sequence-type recognition for 12.3.1, nth-term-of-arithmetic as genuine partial for 12.4.1, and arc/sector naming 9.1.1's head clause.

rejects.reason: 'Solving Algebraic Inequalities with 1 Inequality Sign' is the GCSE linear-inequality lesson; spec 2.5 is 'Find the solution set for quadratic inequalities either graphically or algebraically' (2.5.1 '–3 < x < 4' is an example solution-set form). Same word 'inequalities', different topic (linear vs quadratic); the row's evidence even describes 'two inequality signs', mismatching this video. Keyword-adjacent; rejected at low.

Same video: 'x < 1 or x > 6' is the solution-set example shape of a quadratic inequality, not the topic of a single-sign linear-inequality lesson; quadratic-inequality work is not title-evidenced. Keyword-adjacent; rejected at low.

'Solving Algebraic Inequalities with 2 Inequality Signs' teaches compound linear inequalities (e.g. 1 < 2x+1 < 7); the resemblance to 2.5.1's '–3 < x < 4' example form is surface-only — the spec's distinctive content is quadratic inequalities solved graphically or algebraically. Keyword-adjacent; rejected at low.
Same video: compound-linear double inequalities are not the 'x < 1 or x > 6' quadratic solution-set topic of 2.5.2; no quadratic inequality work is title-evidenced. Keyword-adjacent; rejected at low.

'GCSE Physics - Resolving Vectors & Scale Drawing | How to Find Resultant Forces' names force resultants and scale drawing; 13.3.2 is 'solving problems using vector geometry, with a diagram given in more complex cases' (equating like vectors, unknown scalars) — vector geometry is not named and the evidence itself concedes the video is physics-branded. Keyword-adjacent on 'vectors', bound to the wrong sub-clause of 13.3; rejected at low.
